newsitem.title: USA: Unocal, Sun both report better earnings.
newsitem.headline: Unocal, Sun both report better earnings.

text.p: Unocal Corp. reported a 16 percent increase in first-quarter profits Thursday while Sun Co. Inc. said it returned to profitability after a year-earlier loss.

Unocal, an independent oil and gas exploration and production company, said its net income for the three months ended March 31 expanded to $144 million, or 57 cents a share, from $124 million, or 47 cents a share, in the year-ago period.

Sun, one of the nation's largest independent refiners and marketers of petroleum products, posted net income of $18 million, or 10 cents a share, after recording a loss of $5 million, or 22 cents a share, a year ago.

Unocal, which has major oil and natural gas production operations in Asia and the Gulf of Mexico, said increased natural gas production, particularly in Asia, helped to push revenues up to $1.46 billion from $1.20 billion.
The company, which is based in El Segundo, Calif., said its natural gas production in Asia expanded by 35 percent.
It also said that its results were helped significantly by higher average sales prices for crude oil and natural gas.
Sun, which is based in Philadelphia, said its revenues edged up to $2.74 billion from $2.47 billion.

Sun, which operates five refineries, said its earnings were helped by higher production levels, particularly of high-value fuels and chemicals products, and lower absolute costs for its refining operations.

The company, which sells gasoline under the Sunoco brand through more than 3,800 outlets in 17 states, added that higher retail gasoline margins and higher chemical margins also contributed to the improved earnings, which were hurt by a $21 million after-tax charge for employee terminations.
Sun said its earning were also adversely impacted by the high cost of a chemical additive for gasoline and by lower results from its lubricants business.
Sun's stock gained 50 cents to $25 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange while Unocal added 12.5 cents to $37.625, also on the NYSE.
